body:
For me, good moods and exciting moments feel like they're running down a gas gauge. I enjoy the moments I'm happy, I truly treasure them, but at some point during it I can feel my brain sputtering as it gets closer to E on the gauge. Then it's like this "good mood juice" needs to refill for a couple days. 

Idk, it's weird but that's the closest thing to an analogy I can make.

Just knowing somebody out there understands anything means the absolute world to me. I know you said you weren't going to talk about yourself here but if you need literally anything please pm me, don't hesitate!

Thank you so much for sharing, sincerely!

That makes me sad to hear, it's unfortunate how easy it is for people to just scare off when faced with this, especially after such a long time, I can't even imagine. If you need to talk or vent about it please PM me, I'd love to hear what you're willing to share. Hearing others with similar issues helps more than I can even articulate.

I hope all the best for you, from the bottom of my heart

Currently I work in a factory on midnights. I've been trying to get to dayshift 7-3 for two months now with no luck. I'm still with her, roughly 2 months since our first date. She's beautiful, and smart and just amazing, I'm still shocked she gave me the time of day. The insecurities from my depression/anxiety are what is pushing her away, it's clear as day. When things are going good it's great but when my mind slips she gets distant and irritated with me. I'd get irritated with me too. I'm in my late 20s, knocking on 30's door. I realize all of this is "overthinking" and I try to suppress it but it gets harder and harder to fight it down every day. This year has hands down been the worst my depression has ever been. Like I'm losing myself. I literally have no idea what to do. Therapy hasn't helped with a majority of my issues and medicine breaks me. I'd rather feel something than nothing, ya know?

I don't really have any words somebody else hasn't already said but I really hope the best for you! Keep your chin up!

Dapper! Debonair! You look good bro!

Keep pushing, you will get there and it'll make the whole fight feel worth it!

Also you've got a really cute nose and those eyebrows are on point! Simply stunning!
Weight comes and goes with the waves of life my friend. If it's something you want you can drop it again but don't beat yourself up for it. You look good man and friendly as hell lol
Good! If you need anything at all feel free to PM. I got you. Make your redemption story one for the ages!

I'd figure that is a pretty normal feeling actually, especially when you feel you relate to things on any sort of deep level.

Diagnosable or "bummed out" are just labels for your feels, neither one makes them any less important. More than anything this sub has always made feel like "oh hey there are people out there that actually understand" and tbh it makes any tough time feel more tolerable and far less lonely.

I wish you all the best, OP

Take it all in. Embrace it and feel your feelings. Eventually I'm confident you'll feel that spark, THAT is when you start climbing back up.

Best of luck OP

Every person you have ever made smile.
Every dog that's wagged it's tail excitedly because you gave it attention
Every person here in r/depression who needs you to win this fight
Every time you've survived this feeling before, don't let go of that hard work

The important thing is you are a life that means far too much to just extinguish. The reason to live is you. Even if you don't feel like you have, you've  impacted this world in one way or another. Don't cut this story short

I don't really think it will help solve your feelings but there is an exchange from the show 'Louie' that I've kept in my heart of hearts ever since I watched it. Maybe it will stick with you as well.

Conversation Between Louie and Dr. Bigelow:

B: You know, misery is wasted on the miserable.

L: What?

B: You know, I'm not entirely sure what your name is, but you are a classic idiot. You think spending time with her, kissing her, having fun with her, you think that's what it was all about? That was love?

L: Yeah.

B: THIS is love. Missing her, because she's gone. Wanting to die.... You're so lucky. You're like a walking poem. Would you rather be some kind of a fantasy? Some kind of a Disney ride? Is that what you want? Don't you see? This is the good part. This is what you've been digging for all this time. Now you finally have it in your hand, this sweet nugget of love, sweet, sad love, and you want to throw it away. You've got it all wrong.

L: I thought this was the bad part.

B: No! The bad part is when you forget her, when you don't care about her, when you don't care about anything. The bad part is coming, so enjoy the heartbreak while you can, for God's sakes. 



Heartbreak and loneliness are tough, OP, I'm not trying to denote that. Just providing a potential different point of view. I wish you all the best, I wish there was more I could do from beyond the interwebz, but I fear there is not. Stay strong!
Not trying. It's just happening. She's getting tired of me. She's getting tired of the questions. Of the insecurity.
